[[Direct Line Group]] | num_employees = 36,000 (2026){{cite web|url=https://www.aviva.com/investors/annual-report//|title=Annual report|publisher=Aviva|access-date=27 March 2026}} | founded = {{start date|2000|5|30|df=y}} | hq_location = [[London]], England, UK | area_served = {{Unbulleted list|United Kingdom|Ireland|Canada|China|India}} | website = {{official URL}} }} '''Aviva''' is a British [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[insurance]] company headquartered in [[London]], England. It has about 25.2 million customers in the United Kingdom, Ireland and Canada.{{cite web |title=About us |url=https://www.aviva.com/about-us/our-people/ |access-date=27 March 2025 |website=Aviva.com |publisher=Aviva plc}} In the United Kingdom, Aviva is the largest general insurer and a leading life and pensions provider. Aviva is also the second-largest general insurer in Canada. Aviva has a primary listing on the [[London Stock Exchange]], and is a constituent of the [[FTSE 100 Index]]. ==Name== The name of the company upon its formation in May 2000 was CGNU plc and was created when [[Norwich Union]] merged with insurer [[CGU plc]].{{Cite book|author1=Gary Armstrong|author2=Michael Harker|author3=Philip Kotler|author4=Ross Brennan|title=Marketing: An Introduction|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UNd1Bm9l6KUC|year=2009|isbn=978-0-273-71395-1|publisher=Pearson Education|page=246}} In April 2002, the company's shareholders voted to change the company name to '''Aviva plc''', an invented [[palindrome]] word derived from "viva", the Latin for 'alive' and designed to be short, memorable and work worldwide. The new company's logo incorporated a triangle, which is based on the spire of Norwich Cathedral. The Norwich Union brand was retained for the UK long-term savings and general insurance business.{{cite news|url=http://www.scotsman.com/business/changing-the-name-of-the-game-1-1432727#|title=Changing the name of the game |access-date=15 September 2012|publisher=The Scotsman|date=3 May 2008}} In April 2008, Aviva announced that it would adopt the Aviva name as its worldwide consumer-facing brand, and that the Norwich Union brand would be phased out in the United Kingdom.{{cite news|url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-aviva-brand-idUKL2940636020080429|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160108102942/http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-aviva-brand-idUKL2940636020080429|url-status=dead|archive-date=8 January 2016|title=Aviva scraps Norwich Union name|access-date=15 September 2012|work=Reuters|date=29 April 2008|first=Clara|last=Ferreira-Marques}} ==History== Aviva can trace its history back to the establishment of the [[Hand in Hand Fire & Life Insurance Society]] in London in 1696.{{cite web|title=Aviva Heritage Events Timeline|url=http://www.aviva.com/about-us/heritage/events-timeline/non-flash/|publisher=Aviva plc|access-date=29 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120917194123/http://www.aviva.com/about-us/heritage/events-timeline/non-flash/|archive-date=17 September 2012|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}Note: taken over by Commercial Union in 1905 [[File:Gas Lamp no. 313 London and Lancashire Fire and Life in Dublin.jpg|thumbnail|left|Predecessor company London and Lancashire Fire and Life, pictured in Dublin, {{Circa|1871}}]] It was created by a merger of two British insurance firms, [[Norwich Union]] and [[CGU plc]]{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/649600.stm|title=CGU and Norwich Union merge | publisher=BBC News | date=21 February 2000}} (itself created by the merger of 1998 of [[Commercial Union]] and [[General Accident]]{{Cite web |url=http://www.aviva.com/about-us/heritage/countries/ireland |title=About Us > Heritage |publisher=Aviva.com |access-date=12 November 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141112123142/http://www.aviva.com/about-us/heritage/countries/ireland/ |archive-date=12 November 2014 |url-status=dead }}) as CGNU in February 2000. The Aviva name was adopted in July 2002.{{Cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/4492729/Why-only-Avivas-directors-will-be-living-well-Come-back-Vasco-da-Gama-your-country-needs-you-Bios-golden-goose-is-in-danger-of-becoming-a-turkey.html |title=Why only Aviva's directors will be 'living well' |work=The Telegraph|date=19 March 2002 |access-date=24 March 2012 |location=London}} Thereafter, most of the group operations, except for some strong local brands, were carried out under the uniform brand "Aviva".{{cite web |url=http://www.checksure.biz/ftse_100_companies/aviva.asp |title=Aviva PLC |access-date=26 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130428002306/http://www.checksure.biz/ftse_100_companies/aviva.asp |archive-date=28 April 2013 |url-status=dead }} In 2002, Aviva purchased Abeille Vie, a In March 2005, Aviva acquired the [[RAC plc]] breakdown recovery operation for around £1.1 billion.{{Cite web |url=http://www.racnews.co.uk/index.asp?pageid=13 |title=RAC History 2025|newspaper=Aviva|access-date=2 July 2025}} ===Constituent companies=== Aviva is the result of the merger of hundreds of insurance companies over several centuries.{{cite web |url=https://www.aviva.com/about-us/our-heritage/legacy-companies/ |title=Legacy companies |website=Aviva}} Aviva was originally formed as CGNU from the merger of CGU and Norwich Union. ====CGU==== {{main|CGU plc}} CGU was formed in 1998 from the merger of Commercial Union and General Accident.{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB888413884754700500|title=U.K.'s Commercial Union, General Accident to Merge|publisher=The Wall Street Journal|date=26 February 1998|access-date=18 April 2020}} =====Commercial Union===== {{main|Commercial Union}} The Commercial Union Assurance Company was founded in 1861 as a result of insurance premium increases following the [[1861 Tooley Street fire]].Liveing, Edward. '' A Century of Insurance: The Commercial Union Assurance Group 1861 - 1961''. London: H F & G Witherby, 1961 ======Hand in Hand====== {{main|Hand in Hand Fire and Life Insurance Society}} The Hand in Hand Fire and Life Insurance Society was established in 1696 as the Contributors for Insuring Houses, Chambers or Rooms from Loss by Fire, by Amicable Contribution. The name Hand in Hand came from its logo of two joined hands underneath a crown. In 1905 it became part of Commercial Union, at which time it was the oldest insurer in the UK.{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/stream/accountoffireins00reltuoft/accountoffireins00reltuoft_djvu.txt|title=An account of the fire insurance companies associations, institutions, projects and schemes established and projected in Great Britain and Ireland during the 17th and 18th centuries including the Sun Fire Office; also of Charles Povey the projector of that office, his writings and schemes|first=Francis Boyer|last=Relton|publisher=Swan Sonnenschein & Co.|year=1893}} ======British General====== The British General Insurance Company was established in 1904. It became part of Commercial Union in 1926.{{cite web|url=https://insurancehistory.cii.co.uk/collections_firemark/british-general-insurance-company-ltd/|title=British General Insurance Company Ltd|publisher=Chartered Insurance Institute|access-date=16 December 2025}} ======Northern and Employers====== The Northern and Employers Assurance Company was formed in 1960 from the Northern Assurance Company and the Employers' Liability Assurance Company. It was acquired by Commercial Union in 1968.{{cite web|url=https://www.rhodesianstudycircle.org.uk/the-northern-assurance-company-limited/|title=The Northern Assurance Company Limited|publisher=Rhodesian Study Circle|access-date=16 December 2025}} ======Employers' Liability Assurance====== The Employers' Liability Assurance Corporation was established in 1880, the first company to offer employers' liability insurance. It became part of the Northern and Employers Assurance Company in 1960.{{cite web|url=https://museums.bristol.gov.uk/narratives.php?irn=16100|title=Employers' Liability Assurance Corporation Ltd|publisher=Bristol Museum|access-date=16 December 2025}} ======Northern Assurance====== {{anchor|Northern Assurance Company Act 1848|Northern Assurance Amendment Act 1861|Northern Assurance Act 1865|Northern Assurance Act 1874|Northern Assurance Act 1889|Northern Assurance Act 1899|Northern Assurance Act 1908}} The North of Scotland Fire and Life Assurance Company was formed in Aberdeen in 1836, and took the name Northern Assurance Company in 1848. It became part of the Northern and Employers Assurance Company in 1960.{{cite web|url=https://archiveshub.jisc.ac.uk/search/archives/2af6fe45-f7c0-3e05-8444-5d4adabbc2fc|title=Records of the Northern Assurance Company Ltd|publisher=Archives Hub|access-date=16 December 2025}} ======White Cross====== The White Cross Insurance Association was founded in 1906. Originally called the Red Cross Indemnity Assurance Company it was renamed in 1912 due to the restrictions on the red cross name and symbol placed by international law. It became part of Commercial Union in 1968.{{cite book|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=tSAYeP8at1MC |title= The Stock Exchange Gazette|volume=26|year=1926 |page=1627|quote=This company was established in 1906 as the Red Cross Indemnity Association for the insurance of motor cars}} ======North British and Mercantile====== {{main|North British and Mercantile Insurance}} The North British and Mercantile Insurance Company (originally the North British Fire Office) was founded in 1809. It merged with the Mercantile Fire Insurance Company in 1862, and became part of Commercial Union in 1959.{{cite web|url=https://museums.bristol.gov.uk/narratives.php?irn=16114|title=North British & Mercantile|publisher=Bristol Museum|access-date=16 December 2025}} ======Railway Passengers====== {{anchor|Railway Passengers Assurance Company Act 1849|Railway Passengers Assurance Company's Act 1852|Railway Passengers Assurance Company's Act 1864|Railway Passengers Assurance Act 1881|Railway Passengers Assurance Act 1897|Railway Passengers Assurance (Consolidation) Act 1918|Railway Passengers Assurance Act 1959}} The Universal Railway Casualty Compensation Company was formed in 1848 to insure travellers against accidents on the rapidly developing railways. This made it the first company established specifically to provide accident insurance. Later renamed the Railway Passengers Assurance Company, it became part of the North British and Mercantile Insurance Company in 1910.{{cite web|url=https://museumofscottishrailways.org.uk/insurance-tickets-sign/|title=Insurance Tickets Sign|publisher=Museum of Scottish Railways|access-date=16 December 2025}}{{Cite web |title=Railway Passengers Assurance Company |url=https://archives.cie.ie/names/760396b0-7797-47a5-b8e6-6b502aadb0db |access-date=2026-03-27 |website=CIÉ Group Archives Catalogue |language=en-gb}} ======West of England Fire and Life====== The West of England Fire and Life Insurance Company was founded in 1807 in Exeter. It was acquired by Commercial Union in 1897.{{cite web|url=https://www.exetermemories.co.uk/em/_commercial/westengland.php|title=West Of England Fire and Life Insurance Company|publisher=Exeter Memories|access-date=17 December 2025}} =====General Accident===== {{main|General Accident}} The General Accident and Employers' Liability Assurance Association was founded in 1885. In 1891 its business was taken over by a new entity, General Accident Fire and Life Assurance Corporation. General Accident was one of the first insurers to offer motor insurance, issuing its first policy in 1896.Irvine Gray, A Business Epic 1885-1935, 1935 ======General Life====== The General Life Assurance Company (originally the Protestant Dissenters' and General Life and Fire Assurance Company) was formed in 1837, and became part of General Accident in 1925.{{cite web|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/pdf/2339074.pdf|title=Fires and Fire Insurance Considered Under their Historical, Financial, Statistical, and National Aspects|first=Cornelius|last= Walford|page=396|publisher= Journal of the Statistical Society of London|volume=40|date=1 September 1877|access-date=16 December 2025}} ======Yorkshire Insurance====== The Yorkshire Fire and Life Insurance Company was founded in 1824. It was acquired by General Accident in 1968.{{cite web |title=Yorkshire Fire and Life Insurance Company |url=https://collection.sciencemuseumgroup.org.uk/people/ap27220/yorkshire-fire-and-life-insurance-company |website=Science Museum Group |access-date=9 December 2022}} =====Gresham===== Gresham Insurance Company (originally the Gresham Fire and Accident Insurance Society) was founded in 1910. It became part of CGU in 2005.{{cite web|url=https://insurancehistory.cii.co.uk/collections_firemark/gresham-fire-accident-insurance-society/|title=Gresham Fire & Accident Insurance Society|publisher=Chartered Insurance Institute|access-date=16 December 2025}} ====Norwich Union==== {{main|Norwich Union}} Norwich Union Fire Insurance Society (originally the Norwich Union Society for Insuring of Buildings, Goods, Merchandises & Effects from Loss by Fire) was established in 1797. It was renamed Norwich Union Insurance in 1997.{{cite web|url=http://www.oxforddnb.com/view/article/48249 |title=Thomas Bignold |publisher= Oxford Dictionary of National Biography|access-date=16 December 2025}} =====Norwich and London===== The Norwich and London Accident Insurance Association (originally the Norwich and London Accident and Casualty Insurance Association) was founded in 1856. It became part of Norwich Union Fire Insurance Society in 1909.{{cite book|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=IDsQAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA42 |title= The Insurance Register, Containing a Record of the Yearly Progress and the Present Financial Position of British Life Assurance Associations|year=1893|publisher=Layton|page=42}}{{Cite web |title=Timeline |url=https://www.aviva.com/about-us/our-heritage/timeline/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251117222548/https://www.aviva.com/about-us/our-heritage/timeline/ |archive-date=2025-11-17 |access-date=2026-03-27 |website=www.aviva.com |language=en-GB}} ======General Hail Storm====== The General Hail Storm Insurance Society was established in 1843 to insure crops and glass against damage from hail. It became part of the Norwich and London Accident Insurance Association in 1909.{{cite book|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=0jcQAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA24 |title=The Insurance Register, Containing a Record of the Yearly Progress and the Present Financial Position of British Life Assurance Associations|year=1876|publisher=Layton|page=24}} ====Friends Life==== {{main|Friends Life Group}} Friends Life was formed in 2011 from a combination of Friends Provident, the majority of AXA's life insurance business, and Bupa. It became part of Aviva in 2015.{{Cite news|url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/idUKL0143575220080501|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100704092320/http://uk.reuters.com/article/idUKL0143575220080501|url-status=dead|archive-date=4 July 2010|title=Resolution's Cowdery eyes restructuring venture|last=Ferreira-Marques|first=Clara|date=1 May 2008|work=Reuters |accessdate=8 November 2009}} =====Friends Provident===== {{main|Friends Provident}} Friends Provident was formed in 1832 by Quakers in Yorkshire. It became part of Friends Life in 2011.David Tregoning & Hugh Cockerell, Friends' Provident Life Office 1832-1982, London, 1982 ====Direct Line==== {{main|Direct Line Group}} Direct Line was formed in 2012 from the insurance business of Royal Bank of Scotland. It became part of Aviva in 2025.{{cite news |title=Direct Line nears RBS separation |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-scotland-business-19463398 |newspaper=BBC News |date=3 September 2012 |access-date=3 September 2012}} ==Operations== [[File:AvivaCanadaMarkhamHeadquarters4.jpg|thumb|Aviva Canada]] Aviva's main activities are the provision of general and life insurance, long term savings products and fund management services. The group has around 36,000 employees and 25.2 million customers. Aviva Investors has £262 billion assets under management as of 31 December 2025.{{Cite web |last=Kenway |first=Natalie |date=2026-03-05 |title=Aviva Investors delivers 200% jump in net flows for 2025 |url=https://portfolio-adviser.com/aviva-investors-delivers-200-jump-in-net-flows-for-2025/ |access-date=2026-03-27 |website=Portfolio Adviser |language=en-US}} ===Principal subsidiaries=== {{div col|colwidth=22em}} *United Kingdom ** Insurance, Wealth & Retirement ** Aviva Insurance – General Insurance (including the Quotemehappy brand) ** [[Aviva Investors]] – Fund Management ''(formerly Morley)'' *Canada – [[Aviva Canada]] *China – Aviva-Cofco *India – Aviva India *Ireland **[[Aviva Ireland|Aviva Direct]] **[[Hibernian Aviva Health|Aviva Health]] {{div col end}} ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== {{Portal|London|Companies|Banks}} *{{Official|https://www.aviva.com}} *{{PM20|FID=co/004650|TEXT=Clippings about|NAME=Commercial Union Assurance Company}} {{Aviva}} {{Navboxes|list1= {{FTSE 100 Index constituents}} {{DJSI World}} {{Major_insurance_companies}} {{ICISA members}} }} {{authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Aviva Plc}} [[Category:Aviva| ]] [[Category:Financial services companies established in 2000]] [[Category:Companies listed on the London Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Companies in the FTSE 100 Index]] [[Category:Companies formerly listed on the New York Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Financial services companies based in the City of London]] [[Category:Multinational companies based in the City of London]] [[Category:British brands]]
extract:
Aviva is a British multinational insurance company headquartered in London, England. It has about 25.2 million customers in the United Kingdom, Ireland and Canada. In the United Kingdom, Aviva is the largest general insurer and a leading life and pensions provider. Aviva is also the second-largest general insurer in Canada.
Aviva has a primary listing on the London Stock Exchange, and is a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index.
